finding.title: Add ref.mounted guards after awaits in PinFlowController before touching state

evidence.quote:
try {
          final ok = await pinService.verifyProfilePin(profileId, pin);

state = state.copyWith(busy: true, errorMessage: null);
        await pinService.setProfilePin(profileId, pin);

try {
      final ok = await pinService.verifyProfilePin(profileId, pin);

finding.why: Per SM-4 (and the digest's own note that Riverpod 3 throws UnmountedRefException), every `await` in a Notifier method must be followed by a `ref.mounted` check before touching `state`. None of the four PIN-transition handlers in this @Riverpod(keepAlive:true) notifier do this — `_handleSetup`, `_handleChange` (twice), and `_handleVerify` all assign `state = state.copyWith(...)` immediately after an `await pinService.*Pin(...)` with no guard. The confirm-step of `_handleChange` (line 350-351) is worse: it has no try/catch at all around `setProfilePin`, unlike its own sibling handlers. If the provider is invalidated/torn down while a bcrypt hash/secure-storage write is in flight (e.g. rapid navigation away, container disposal), the resulting exception is unguarded and, for the confirm-step case, has no catch clause to even convert it to a value.
finding.recommendation: After each await in _handleSetup/_handleChange/_handleVerify, add `if (!ref.mounted) return;` before assigning state; wrap the confirm-step setProfilePin call in the same try/catch pattern used by _handleSetup.
acceptance_criteria: Every await in pin_flow_controller.dart's four handlers is followed by a ref.mounted check before state is touched
A regression test disposes the ProviderContainer mid-await and asserts no UnmountedRefException escapes
_handleChange's confirm step catches the same exception types as _handleSetup

finding.title: Log swallowed exceptions in profiles' log-less catch blocks instead of silently discarding them

evidence.quote:
} catch (_) {
      // no-op: cloud push failure is non-fatal; local write already succeeded (offline-first)

} catch (_) {
      // no-op: cloud push failure is non-fatal; local write already succeeded (offline-first)

} catch (_) {
      // no-op: cloud push failure is non-fatal; local write already succeeded.

finding.why: Five catch blocks across this batch swallow exceptions with zero AppLogger call — three in profile_repository_impl.dart discard cloud-sync push failures (create/update/self-heal) with only a code comment, and two more (profile_picker_screen.dart, add_profile_dialog.dart) silently clear a live duplicate-name validation error on any DB exception. add_profile_dialog.dart's own line 269-280 shows the correct pattern (AppLogger.instance.error with event/exception/stackTrace) right next to one of the log-less ones, proving the gap is an oversight, not a style choice. Without logging, a real production failure pattern (e.g. outbox writes silently failing on a subset of devices) leaves no telemetry trail to diagnose from.
finding.recommendation: Replace each `catch (_) { ... }` with a catch that logs via AppLogger.instance.warning/error (event + exception) before continuing with the existing non-fatal behavior.
acceptance_criteria: All 5 listed catch blocks call AppLogger before continuing
A grep-based Rule-0 check (or custom_lint rule, once custom_lint is unblocked) flags `catch (_) {` / `catch (e) {` blocks in lib/ with no AppLogger call in their body

finding.title: Guard ProfileRepositoryImpl.deleteProfile's cloud-sync push the same way create/update/ensureDefaultProfile do
finding.why: createProfile, updateProfile, and ensureDefaultProfile all wrap their `_syncEngine?.push*` call in try/catch with an explicit 'offline-first, cloud push is non-fatal' comment. deleteProfile does not: `await _syncEngine?.deleteLearnerProfile(id)` runs bare, after the local cascade-delete transaction has already committed across ~12 tables. Both push and delete enqueue through the same outbox `_enqueue` mechanism (a local Drift insert), so they carry the same theoretical failure mode (e.g. disk-full, DB-locked). If that insert throws, the whole deleteProfile Future rejects even though the profile is already gone locally — and neither of deleteProfile's two callers in this batch (profile_edit_delete_actions.dart's deleteProfileFlow, profile_picker_screen.dart's _showDeleteDialog) catch it either, so the exception surfaces as an unhandled error in a button's onPressed handler while the delete has, in fact, already succeeded — contradicting the offline-first invariant this same file documents for every other mutation.
finding.recommendation: Wrap `await _syncEngine?.deleteLearnerProfile(id)` in the same non-fatal try/catch (with logging per the previous finding) used by createProfile/updateProfile/ensureDefaultProfile.
acceptance_criteria: deleteProfile's sync call is wrapped in try/catch matching its siblings, with a logged, non-fatal failure
A test with a SyncWriteFacade fake that throws on deleteLearnerProfile asserts ProfileRepositoryImpl.deleteProfile still completes normally

finding.title: Convert ProfileSession to @freezed instead of hand-written ==/hashCode
finding.rule: naming/placement — domain/state models are @freezed, never hand-written ==/hashCode
finding.why: ProfileSession is a domain/state model living under domain/models/ (the same directory as the correctly-@freezed ProfileModel), but hand-writes operator== and hashCode instead of using @freezed as the coding standard requires. Today's implementation looks correct, but hand-rolled equality is exactly the class of bug (forgotten field, inconsistent hashCode) the @freezed rule exists to prevent, and it's inconsistent with its own sibling file in the same directory.
finding.recommendation: Convert ProfileSession to an abstract @freezed class with a private const constructor for the isActive getter, matching ProfileModel's pattern.
acceptance_criteria: ProfileSession is declared @freezed; dart run build_runner build generates profile_session.freezed.dart
Existing call sites (ProfileSession(profileId:), .none(), .isActive) keep compiling unchanged

finding.title: Split four hand-written files in features/profiles that exceed the 400-line AG-3 cap
finding.why: AG-3 caps hand-written Dart files at 400 lines; four files in this batch exceed it: pin_flow_controller.dart (416), parent_settings_screen.dart (612), profile_picker_screen.dart (539), parent_pin_keypad_dialog.dart (635). Each mixes multiple concerns in one file (e.g. parent_pin_keypad_dialog.dart holds two full dialog state machines plus the shared keypad/dots/lockout widgets; parent_settings_screen.dart holds the screen plus a full points-adjustment dialog plus two private widget classes), making them harder to navigate and increasing merge-conflict surface.
finding.recommendation: Extract private widget/dialog classes into their own files (e.g. move _ManageRow/_WhitePanel and the points-adjust dialog out of parent_settings_screen.dart; move _PinKeypad/_PinDotsRow/_LockoutPanel out of parent_pin_keypad_dialog.dart).
acceptance_criteria: All four files are at or under 400 lines
The AG-3 line-count checker (once it exists per Rule 0) passes for features/profiles
